title: M2 — Loop verified (agent core)
source: SPECIFICATION.md §5 (the agent core), §3 (agent_message / agent_event data model), §12 (loop_driver + Faux_provider). Milestone M2: the agent loop wired to a scriptable faux provider; no real network. Exercises the full turn-and-hook surface, tool-execution ordering, and cancellation. The §6 Agent wrapper is explicitly OUT of scope for M2 (deferred to the harness, M5).

baseline.notes:
M1 (provider layer) is merged to main at 091379d; dune build and dune runtest are green. Libraries present: pera_types (data model), pera_provider (Provider.S, Event_stream, SSE parser/interpreter, Json_schema, Json_repair, Anthropic_provider, anthropic_request, provider_driver). No pera_core library exists yet — it is created in this milestone.

DESIGN DECISIONS settled with the user before planning (do not revisit without asking):
(1) SCOPE — bare loop only. Build the loop, hooks, tool execution, Faux_provider, and loop_driver. The §6 Agent wrapper (subscription fan-out, single-flight, observable state) is deferred to the harness milestone (M5).
(2) TOOL RESULTS — add a third ToolResultMessage variant to Provider.message (pi-faithful: Message = UserMessage | AssistantMessage | ToolResultMessage), and teach anthropic_request to render it. Anthropic requires consecutive tool-result messages to be COALESCED into a single user-role message carrying multiple tool_result content blocks (ref vendor/pi/packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts lines 1100-1133). build_request_body's current 1:1 List.map over messages must become a grouping fold.
(3) HTTP_CLIENT — extract a thin Http_client abstraction in M2 (Stage 1), resolving the noted issue from the PR #2 review on anthropic_provider.ml:119 (piaf body/error types leaking into the provider). Wrap piaf behind: type body, fold_body_string, type error / error_to_string.
(4) LOOP↔PROVIDER SEAM — the loop config takes a provider-agnostic stream_fn closure (model/context/options/sw -> Event_stream.t), NOT a Provider.S module. This keeps the loop pure-from-IO and free of ~env. Faux_provider satisfies Provider.S AND exposes an adapter that produces a stream_fn; the harness/driver binds ~env into the closure.

REUSE AUDIT (modules this plan creates vs. existing code):
- Event_stream (pera_provider): REUSE as-is at the agent-core level — spec §4 says the same ('event,'result) t carries (agent_event, agent_message list) inside the loop. No change needed.
- Provider.message / Provider.context / Provider.simple_stream_options (pera_provider): REUSE; extend message with ToolResultMessage (Stage 2).
- assistant_message_event, assistant_message, tool_call, tool_result_content, stop_reason, model, tool_error (pera_types): REUSE; the agent core builds history and events from these.
- Json_schema.validate (pera_provider): REUSE for tool-argument validation before execute (Stage 6).
- Json_repair: not needed at this layer.
- agent_message, agent_event, 'ctx tool, tool_output, agent_loop_config, hooks, the run function, Faux_provider, loop_driver: ALL NEW (pera_core).
- Ported from pi: the loop control flow and tests come from vendor/pi/packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts and vendor/pi/packages/agent/test/agent-loop.test.ts. Type shapes from vendor/pi/packages/agent/src/types.ts (AgentEvent lines 403-418, AgentLoopConfig lines 135-277). The Agent class (agent.ts) and agent.test.ts are §6 wrapper material — NOT ported in M2.

LAYERING NOTE: agent_message/agent_event reference Provider.message, which lives in pera_provider (not pera_types). Therefore the agent-core data types must live in pera_core (which depends on pera_provider), not in pera_types. The 'ctx tool type references Eio.Switch/Eio.Cancel, so it also belongs in pera_core.

epochs.title: Provider-layer prerequisites for the loop
epochs.description: Two pera_provider changes the loop depends on, both flagged as noted issues. Stage 1 extracts the Http_client abstraction (PR #2 review debt); it is independent of the loop. Stage 2 adds the ToolResultMessage variant and tool-result serialisation (coalescing) so the loop can feed tool results back through convert_to_llm. Both compile and keep the existing provider tests green.

stages.title: Extract Http_client abstraction in pera_provider
stages.description: Introduce a thin Http_client module that wraps piaf, so the Anthropic provider no longer references Piaf.Body / Piaf.Error directly. Resolves the noted refactor hazard from the PR #2 review (anthropic_provider.ml:119) and the spec's Open Question #11. Behaviour-preserving: the provider's observable output does not change.
stages.implementation_notes: Read anthropic_provider.ml first to see exactly which piaf surfaces it uses (look for Piaf.Body.*, Piaf.Error.*, the request/post call, the streaming body fold). Define Http_client.mli to expose only what the provider needs, hiding piaf: at minimum (a) a way to issue a streaming POST that yields response body chunks to a callback under a switch, and (b) error normalisation. Suggested surface: `type error`; `val error_to_string : error -> string`; a `post_stream` (or `stream_response`) function taking ~env ~sw, url, headers, and body string, plus an ~on_chunk:(string -> unit) callback, returning (unit, error) result; it folds the response body string-by-string into on_chunk (this is where the current Piaf.Body.fold_string / Piaf.Error.to_string usage moves). Keep the signature minimal — do not expose Piaf types in the .mli. Move the piaf-specific code from anthropic_provider.ml into http_client.ml and rewrite the provider to call Http_client. Do NOT change the provider's external behaviour, the SSE pipeline, or Provider.S. open Containers at the top of the .ml. IO returns Result, never raises (guideline pera-specific §6). This is the abstraction the OpenAI-completions provider will share at M3.
coding_guidelines_to_emphasize: module-boundaries.md — .mli hides piaf entirely; the provider sees only Http_client's interface
abstractions.md — one narrow seam over the HTTP library; parameter reduction
error-handling.md — error_to_string maps transport failures to strings; never raise on network errors
pera-specific.md §5 — ~sw labelled arg; structured concurrency

stages.title: ToolResultMessage variant + Anthropic tool-result serialisation
stages.description: Add the third message variant so tool results can live in conversation history and be sent back to the provider. Extend the Anthropic request builder to render tool-result messages, coalescing consecutive ones into a single user-role message with multiple tool_result blocks (Anthropic's required shape).
stages.implementation_notes: In provider.mli, extend the message variant to: UserMessage of Types.user_message | AssistantMessage of Types.assistant_message | ToolResultMessage of Types.tool_result_content. (Types.tool_result_content already exists: { tool_call_id; content: Yojson.Safe.t; is_error: bool }.) This makes every existing match on Provider.message non-exhaustive — fix them (notably anthropic_request.message_to_json) so the build stays green. In anthropic_request.ml: a single ToolResultMessage renders to an Anthropic user message whose content is a list of one tool_result block: { type: 'tool_result', tool_use_id: <tool_call_id>, content: <content>, is_error: <bool> }. CRITICAL: consecutive ToolResultMessages must coalesce into ONE user message carrying all their tool_result blocks (Anthropic rejects tool_result blocks split across separate user messages when they answer one assistant turn's parallel calls). The current build_request_body does `List.map message_to_json context.messages` — a 1:1 map cannot coalesce. Replace that with a grouping pass over the message list (a fold that, when it hits a run of ToolResultMessages, emits a single user message with the collected blocks). Reference vendor/pi/packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts lines 1100-1133 for the exact algorithm (collect current + look ahead while role is toolResult, emit one user message, skip consumed). The content field of tool_result: if Types.tool_result_content.content is already a JSON string value use it directly; otherwise wrap per Anthropic (a JSON value is acceptable as the content of a tool_result block). Update anthropic_request.mli only if a new public function is introduced (e.g. if you expose `messages_to_json : Provider.message list -> Yojson.Safe.t list` for the coalescing pass — preferred over keeping it private if it aids testing). open Containers; no structural equality (match on the variant).
coding_guidelines_to_emphasize: pattern-matching.md — exhaustive match on the now-3-way message variant; no catch-all
type-safety.md — ToolResultMessage carries the typed tool_result_content, not a stringly blob
naming-and-intermediates.md — name the coalescing/grouping step clearly
pera-specific.md — open Containers, no (=) on variants

epochs.title: Agent core loop (pera_core)
epochs.description: Build the pera_core library: the agent data model (agent_message, agent_event, tool, tool_output, loop config + hooks), the Faux_provider test double, the loop control flow (outer/inner loops, streaming consumption, hook contract), tool execution (sequential + parallel with source-ordered results, schema validation, error and deny handling), cancellation, and the loop_driver. At the end of this epoch the loop runs deterministically against scripted scenarios with no network or filesystem, proving the M2 property: turn semantics, hook contract, tool-execution ordering, and cancellation are correct independent of any provider.

stages.title: Faux_provider test double
stages.description: Implement Faux_provider: the load-bearing driver/test infrastructure (spec §12). It emits a programmed sequence of assistant_message_events and resolves to a scripted final assistant_message, with no network. It satisfies Provider.S and also exposes a stream_fn adapter (the form the loop consumes). It records the contexts it was called with, so tests can assert on convert_to_llm output and steering/follow-up injection.
stages.implementation_notes:
Faux_provider drives a deterministic Event_stream of Types.assistant_message_event values then closes with a final Types.assistant_message (spec §12 'Faux_provider'). Public surface:
- A script value: e.g. `type turn_script = { events : Types.assistant_message_event list; final : Types.assistant_message }`.
- `val stream_fn_of_scripts : turn_script list -> stream_fn` where stream_fn has the loop's seam type: model:Types.model -> context:Provider.context -> options:Provider.simple_stream_options -> sw:Eio.Switch.t -> (Types.assistant_message_event, Types.assistant_message) Event_stream.t. Each successive loop call (turn) consumes the next turn_script; this is what lets one scenario script a multi-turn conversation (turn 1 issues tool calls, turn 2 ends). Use a ref/queue captured in the closure to advance through the scripts.
- The stream_fn forks a producer fibre under ~sw that pushes the script's events into an Event_stream (capacity 32) with Event_stream.push, then closes with Event_stream.close final (or close_error for an error script). This mirrors Anthropic_provider's structure — read anthropic_provider.ml for the fork/close pattern.
- Recording: capture each received Provider.context (system, messages, tools, thinking) into a list accessible to tests, so a test can assert what convert_to_llm produced and that steering/follow-up messages were injected.
- Also provide `val as_provider : turn_script list -> (module Provider.S)` satisfying Provider.S (stream_simple takes ~env and ignores it) to demonstrate the Provider.S adapter relationship from §12. The loop itself only ever uses stream_fn; as_provider exists to prove Faux_provider IS a Provider.S and that the adapter from Provider.S to stream_fn is trivial.
- For cancellation tests (stage 7), support a script whose producer blocks before emitting AME_done (e.g. an optional `on_event` hook or a `blocking_after : int` index that makes the producer wait on a never-resolved promise / a condition the test controls) so the test can cancel mid-stream. Keep this minimal; a `~pause:(unit -> unit)` callback invoked between events is sufficient.
open Containers. Fibres under ~sw (pera-specific §5). Define the stream_fn type alias here or in agent_types (wherever the loop config will reference it — keep it in one place; agent_types is a reasonable home).

stages.title: Tool execution (sequential + parallel, ordering, validation, hooks)
stages.description: Wire tool execution into the loop's inner-loop step 4-5. Implement schema validation before execute, before_tool_call (Allow/Deny) and after_tool_call hooks, sequential and parallel execution modes with the source-order result rule, and tool-error-to-tool-result conversion. This is the heart of the M2 'tool execution ordering is correct' property.
stages.implementation_notes:
Port vendor/pi/packages/agent/src/agent-loop.ts executeToolCalls (373-388), executeToolCallsSequential (395-449), executeToolCallsParallel (451-516), prepareToolCall (562-626), executePreparedToolCall (628-663). In the inner loop, when the final assistant message contains AToolCall blocks (stop_reason ToolUse), execute them:

MODE SELECTION (pi 373-388): use config.tool_execution as the default; if ANY called tool has mode `Sequential, force the whole batch sequential. Otherwise parallel.

PER TOOL (prepare then execute):
1. Look up the tool by name in config.tools. Unknown tool -> synthesise an error tool_result (is_error=true, is_user_error=true) and skip execute.
2. Validate args against the tool's Json_schema (Json_schema.validate from pera_provider). On Error -> synthesise an error tool_result (is_error=true, is_user_error=true); do NOT call execute (spec §9, §5 'Schema validation failures do the same').
3. Call before_tool_call (if set) with the call context. Deny msg -> synthesise an error tool_result carrying msg, skip execute (spec §5). Allow -> proceed.
4. Emit AE_tool_execution_start {tool_call_id; tool_name; args}.
5. Call tool.execute ~ctx:config.tool_ctx ~args ~sw ~cancel. Catch ANY exception from execute and convert to an error tool_result (is_error=true, is_user_error=false) — a tool raising is caught and surfaced to the LLM (spec §5 'Tool errors are caught'). (Note: an unhandled exception in a tool fibre that is NOT from execute's contract is a programmer error and may propagate — but execute returning a result or raising a normal exception is handled.)
6. Convert (tool_output, tool_error) result to Types.tool_result_content via the Stage 3 helper.
7. Call after_tool_call (if set) — side-effect only (unit).
8. Emit AE_tool_execution_end {tool_call_id; tool_name; result; is_error}.

SEQUENTIAL (pi 395-449): prepare+execute+finalise each call in source order; emit tool_execution_end immediately after each; results appended in call order.

PARALLEL (pi 451-516): run each allowed call in its own fibre under a SUB-SWITCH (Eio.Switch.run / Fiber.fork). Emit tool_execution_start/end in REAL completion order (as fibres finish). BUT the tool_result_content list appended to history MUST be sorted by the original tool-call index, NOT completion order (spec §5 'ordering matters' — this is the load-bearing rule). Use Fiber.all or fork+promise per call, collect results into an array indexed by source position, then read out in source order.

After execution: append the ordered tool_result_content list to context.messages as Real (Provider.ToolResultMessage ...) entries (one per result, in source order — the anthropic_request coalescing from Stage 2 handles wire merging). Emit AE_turn_end {message; tool_results}. The inner loop then continues (there were tool calls), looping back to stream the next assistant turn with the results in context.

Define the before_tool_call / after_tool_call context record types in agent_loop.mli (or agent_types): before_tool_call_ctx carries the assistant message, the tool_call (id/name/arguments), and the validated args; returns Agent_types.before_tool_call_result. after_tool_call_ctx carries the result and is_error.

To make parallel-vs-sequential OBSERVABLE in tests (pi uses a parallelObserved flag, agent-loop.test.ts 452-545): tools' execute can record start/end timestamps or use an Eio condition so the test can detect concurrent execution. Provide test tools that block on a shared signal to force interleaving.

open Containers; library functions over match; fibres under switches (pera-specific §5).

stages.title: Cancellation propagation
stages.description: Implement and verify cancellation per spec §5 'Cancellation': during an LLM stream, during tool execution, and between turns. Cancellation is observed at the next async point; there is no mid-event cancellation.
stages.implementation_notes:
Spec §5 'Cancellation'. The run already executes under ~sw; cancellation is driven by cancelling that switch's context (Eio.Cancel). Decide and document the cancellation entry point: either run takes an extra ?cancel:Eio.Cancel.t (preferred — explicit, matches spec 'The run takes an Eio.Cancel.t') or cancellation is via cancelling ~sw. If adding ?cancel, run wraps its loop body in Eio.Cancel.sub or checks Eio.Cancel.get_error at the documented boundaries.

Behaviours to implement:
- DURING an LLM stream: cancelling causes the provider stream to abort. With Faux_provider, simulate by cancelling while the producer is paused mid-script (use the Stage 4 ~pause hook). The loop should observe the cancellation (the provider closes the stream with an error / AME_error Aborted), emit AE_turn_end with empty tool_results, then AE_agent_end, then return. The final assistant message carries stop_reason Aborted.
- DURING tool execution: the parallel sub-switch is cancelled; running tool fibres receive cancellation at their next async point. Whatever results completed BEFORE cancellation are still appended in source order, then the run terminates as above (spec §5).
- BETWEEN turns: cancellation is observed at the next hook-call boundary; the loop stops before starting a new turn.

The model is 'cancellation is eventually observed at the next async point' — tests must drive an async point (a fibre yield / a blocked tool) and then cancel. Use Eio.Switch.run with a fibre that cancels after the loop reaches a known point (coordinate via an Eio condition or promise the test controls). Do NOT busy-wait. Foreground sleeps are unavailable; use Eio.Condition or Promise to synchronise the cancel with the loop's progress.

Update agent_loop.mli if run's signature gains ?cancel. open Containers; Eio.Cancel not custom flags (pera-specific §5).
coding_guidelines_to_emphasize: pera-specific.md §5 — Eio.Cancel, structured concurrency; no custom cancellation flags
error-handling.md — Aborted is a typed stop_reason, surfaced cleanly, not an exception out of run
test-patterns.md — synchronise cancel with loop progress via Eio.Condition/Promise, not sleeps
nesting-and-control-flow.md — keep the cancellation checks at documented boundaries, not scattered

stages.title: loop_driver — M2 acceptance proof
stages.description: Build the loop_driver binary (spec §12): drives the loop with Faux_provider through named scenarios and prints the agent_event sequence and final messages, with meaningful exit codes. This is the artifact that demonstrates the M2 property (turn semantics, hook contract, tool ordering, cancellation) observably, with no network or filesystem.
stages.implementation_notes: Mirror provider_driver's shape (bin/drivers/provider_driver.ml) and the test-patterns §7 driver pattern. loop_driver selects a scenario by argv (default: run all). Each scenario constructs a Faux_provider script + an agent_loop_config (with simple in-driver tools, e.g. an echo tool and a counter tool, ctx = a small record or unit), calls Agent_loop.run under Eio_main.run + Eio.Switch.run, consumes the (agent_event, agent_message list) Event_stream via Event_stream.iter printing each event as a structured line (use a to_string/pp for agent_event), and on result prints the final messages. Scenarios to include (each maps to a documented expected outcome, spec §12 Faux_provider list): single text turn; parallel tool calls (show completion-order events vs source-order results); sequential tool calls; tool returning an error; mid-stream cancellation; steering-message injection; follow-up-message handling. Exit 0 if all selected scenarios produced their expected event shapes; exit 1 otherwise (the driver can assert lightly and report mismatches). Add loop_driver to bin/drivers/dune ((libraries pera_core pera_provider pera_types eio_main containers)). The driver is a MANUAL tool and is NOT added to any dune runtest alias (same policy as provider_driver). open Containers.
coding_guidelines_to_emphasize: test-patterns.md §7 — driver exercises the public interface; structured human-readable output; meaningful exit code
naming-and-intermediates.md — name each scenario and its expected outcome
pera-specific.md §5 — Eio_main.run + Switch.run entry; consume the Event_stream under the switch
module-boundaries.md — the driver uses only pera_core's public API (run, config, Faux_provider) — a hard-to-write driver signals a leaky seam
